Returns the color of a pixel of a buffer as an ARGB number: red, green and blue are in the lower three bytes, `(color And $FFFFFF)`, and the top byte is the alpha, which is 255 for the screen. Take the parts apart with `Shr` and `And`. For many pixels, lock the buffer and use [ReadPixelFast](ReadPixelFast).

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Color 200, 100, 50
Plot 10, 10
Local c = ReadPixel(10, 10) And $FFFFFF
Print "Red " + ((c Shr 16) And $FF) + " Green " + ((c Shr 8) And $FF) + " Blue " + (c And $FF)
WaitKey
```
@param x       Horizontal position of the pixel.
@param y       Vertical position of the pixel.
@param buffer  The buffer to read from. Defaults to the current buffer.
@returns The color of the pixel, or 0 if the position is outside of the buffer.
@gap Without a lock the pixel has to be fetched from the graphics card, which makes this slow when it is used for many pixels.
@gap The buffers that [Graphics3D](Graphics3D) makes with a depth above 32 are read as they are stored: with the depth 30 the number is A2R10G10B10 (2 bits of alpha on top, then 10 for each of red, green and blue), and with 64 it is ARGB with 8 bits of each channel (the half floats clamped to 0 to 1), which loses the rest. [ReadPixel64](ReadPixel64) gives the Float16 channels. See [Color depth](Color-Depth).
